items.front: Supreme Court — Articles, inauguration, sanctioned strength?
items.back: Part V, Articles 124-147; inaugurated 28 Jan 1950 (successor to the Federal Court, 1937); sanctioned strength 34 (1 CJI + 33).
items.examPoint: Supreme Court composition — 34 judges including CJI

items.front: Who can increase the number of Supreme Court judges?
What does Article 142 empower the Supreme Court to do?
items.back: Pass any order/decree necessary for 'complete justice' — not constrained by ordinary laws made by Parliament.

items.front: SC's power over Centre-State disputes falls under which jurisdiction?
How is a Supreme Court judge removed?
items.back: Art 124(4): for 'proved misbehaviour or incapacity', by special majority (majority of total membership + 2/3 present & voting in each House); process in Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968.
items.examPoint: Supreme Court judges — tenure, resignation & removal (Article 124(4))

items.front: How is the collegium/NJAC issue settled?
items.back: Judges appointed by the President via the Collegium (CJI + senior judges); the NJAC (99th Amendment) was struck down in 2015.

items.front: Why is HC writ power (Art 226) wider than SC's (Art 32)?
items.back: Art 226 issues writs for FRs AND 'any other purpose' (legal rights); Art 32 is confined to Fundamental Rights.
items.examPoint: High Court writ jurisdiction (Article 226) wider than Article 32

items.front: Can a High Court declare a central law invalid?
items.back: Yes — HCs can review central laws; and constitutional amendments are reviewable on the basic-structure test.
items.examPoint: High Court writ jurisdiction (Article 226) wider than Article 32

items.front: Mandamus and Quo Warranto — key limits/features?
items.back: Mandamus lies against a public authority for a public duty (not private, unless public duty); any interested person can seek Quo Warranto.

items.front: Contempt of court — constitutional and statutory basis?
items.back: Court of Record power (Art 129 SC, Art 215 HC); Contempt of Courts Act 1971 (after H.N. Sanyal Committee) defines civil & criminal contempt — not the Constitution.
items.examPoint: High Court as court of record (Article 215) & superintendence (Article 227)

items.front: NALSA — statutory basis and constitutional anchor?
items.back: Legal Services Authorities Act 1987; gives effect to DPSP Article 39A (free legal aid); issues guidelines to State authorities.
items.examPoint: NALSA, Lok Adalats & Gram Nyayalayas (legal aid, Article 39A)

items.front: 'Custodian of the Constitution' and number of High Courts?
items.back: The Supreme Court is the custodian of the Constitution; India has 25 High Courts.
items.examPoint: Number of High Courts & common High Court (Seventh Amendment 1956)

items.front: AP High Court — when, where, and origin?
items.back: Started 1 Jan 2019 at Amaravati; bifurcated from the common High Court at Hyderabad (which became the Telangana HC). Sanctioned strength 37.
items.examPoint: Andhra Pradesh High Court at Amaravati (established 1 Jan 2019)

items.front: Who appoints District Judges, and under which Article?
items.back: The Governor, in consultation with the High Court — Article 233; the HC controls the subordinate judiciary (Art 235).
items.examPoint: Subordinate courts — Articles 233-237 & appointment of District Judges

items.front: Who regulates legal education and enrolment of advocates?
items.back: The Bar Council of India under the Advocates Act, 1961 — it sets standards of legal education and recognises law degrees for enrolment.
items.examPoint: Bar Councils & Advocates Act 1961 — legal education & enrolment

items.back: Police custody: accused in a police lock-up for interrogation. Judicial custody: accused in jail; police cannot interrogate without the magistrate's permission.

items.front: Scope of Mandamus and Quo Warranto?
items.back: Mandamus does not lie against a private body having no public duty; Quo Warranto can be sought by any person, not only the aggrieved party.
A retired Supreme Court judge may be requested by the CJI, with the President's prior consent, to sit and act as a judge of the Supreme Court.
items.examPoint: Article 128 — recall of a retired Supreme Court judge
